clarity.justification: The three subclaims align closely with their tests: P1 measures “precision/recall of the surprise threshold vs oracle divergence tokens,” P2 measures a defined “suppression ratio,” and P3 compares “Pareto-frontier area, early-only vs all-layer.” The proposal is strongly falsifiable through explicit thresholds, including “precision>=0.6 and recall>=0.6,” “DTR suppression>=0.5 at <=2-point utility loss,” and negative criteria such as “suppression <0.25” or an early-layer gap “>25%.” Some implementation-relevant concepts remain ambiguous: “a contrasting-base model flags true divergence tokens” does not define the flagging rule, “h_early(ref)” does not identify the reference model precisely, and the claim alternates between the student’s “OWN per-token surprise” and the formula “p_teacher(x_i | context).” These gaps prevent a fully clarification-free implementation but do not undermine the otherwise coherent, directional, and quantitatively decidable logic.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is constructing the oracle where “a contrasting-base model flags true divergence tokens”; distribution comparison and token ranking are standard operations, but the exact contrast, divergence statistic, and flagging threshold are not specified, so this requires custom methodological choices rather than an impossible magic step. The named Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B models exist, while LoRA, AdamW, forward hooks, stop-gradient activation losses, token-level weighting, and evaluations such as MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K are supported by mature tooling; however, “KL/liminal distillation” and the precise “h_early(ref)” construction are insufficiently defined. Resources are unusually concrete—“~30k generated per trait,” “~15k kept,” “150 held-out probes,” “5 seeds,” and “LoRA rank 16/alpha 32”—which makes the study readily planable. The refuting branch is runnable because clean distillation, frequency-only, random masking, trait-free data, matched/mismatched bases, non-oracle baselines, and an oracle upper bound are explicitly included, although the custom trait elicitation probes and oracle labeling protocol need additional specification before execution.
